speech_en: Look as closely as you like — checking is the best part!
speech_de: Schaut so genau hin, wie ihr wollt — Nachprüfen ist das Beste!
scenario: A cheerful cartoon meteorite being examined under a big magnifying glass, with the magnified patch showing the segmented shape as what it really is: four rounded bumps fused into the stone, no eyes, no face, no legs. The concept is the JOY OF CHECKING — the rock is happy to be looked at — rather than a debunked rock or a cartoon alien. No planet, no stars, no rocket, no alien anywhere.
prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080.

THIS IS A MACRO CLOSE-UP SHOT, LIKE A ZOOMED-IN PHONE CAMERA PHOTO TAKEN TOO CLOSE. The subject is so close to the "camera" that it does NOT fully fit in the frame: the big rock character is CUT OFF by the LEFT edge and by the BOTTOM edge, and the magnifying glass's handle runs off the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner while the top of its round rim is CUT OFF by the TOP edge. There must be ZERO empty white background space visible anywhere in the image — every part of the 1080x1080 canvas is covered by either black line-art or white space that belongs INSIDE a drawn shape. If you can see plain empty background at any edge, the drawing is WRONG — redo it bigger and closer.

SCENE (draw it oversized, then let the frame crop it): A big cheerful cartoon rock — a chunky, lumpy boulder with blunt corners and a few flat facets, drawn as one bold closed outline with lots of open white space inside for colouring. It has a simple friendly face low on its front: two round dot eyes and a wide happy curved smile, nothing else. It has no arms and no legs. It fills the left two thirds of the picture and is far too big for the frame, so its left side is sliced off by the LEFT edge and its base is sliced off by the BOTTOM edge. Across its surface, draw six or seven simple closed shapes to colour: three or four rounded pebble-like bumps, two blobby patches with a wavy outline, and a couple of short curved crack lines.

Tilted diagonally over the rock's upper right side sits a BIG magnifying glass: one large circle drawn with a bold double rim (two concentric bold lines with white space between them for colouring), and a chunky straight handle with rounded ends running down and to the right, sliced off by the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner. The circle is so big that the top of its rim is sliced off by the TOP edge. The glass is held by nobody — it simply hovers over the rock.

INSIDE the magnifying glass circle, draw the rock's surface hugely enlarged, in the same bold coloring-book line style: a cluster of five or six rounded pebble shapes packed close together and touching, and running across them one short low ridge made of four plain rounded bumps joined end to end in a row, like four pebbles fused together into a caterpillar-shaped hump. That ridge is part of the rock's surface: its bottom edge merges into the pebbles beneath it with no gap and no separate outline underneath. It is a bump in stone. It has NO eyes, NO face, NO mouth, NO legs and NO antennae, and neither do any of the pebbles.

Keep the rest of the background covered by the rock, apart from three or four simple rounded confetti dots near the handle.

STYLE — coloring book line art: BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed. NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black fills anywhere (the eyes may have a small solid pupil only). Simple, cheerful, chunky shapes with open white space INSIDE each shape for colouring.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN:
- Any visible empty white background, wall, sky or margin space — the artwork must be so zoomed-in and oversized that it touches or crosses the left, right, top and bottom edges, with elements literally cut off by the edges.
- ANY starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays, shine lines, glint marks, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, halo of rays, or several lines fanning out from one point anywhere — especially on the magnifying glass lens, which must be plain.
- ANY planet, globe, Mars, crescent, star, starfield, comet tail, rocket, spaceship, flying saucer, astronaut, alien or space helmet anywhere.
- ANY face, eyes or mouth on anything except the big rock itself.
- ANY rectangle, box outline, picture frame, panel edge, border line or vignette around the whole picture.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures, watermarks or writing of any kind anywhere in the image.
- NO speech bubble or thought bubble (added separately afterwards).
- NO human figure, no hand, no arm holding the magnifying glass.
- NO sad, worried, frightened or disappointed expression — the rock is cheerful and curious.

status: DONE, 2 API calls on gemini-2.5-flash-image plus one local crop-and-re-trace (no third call). Attempt 1 was already frame-free, text-free, starburst-free and space-imagery-free, and measured bottom 0.0660 / left 0.0806 / right 0.0157 on the composed page — right just under the 0.02 floor. Its bigger problem was inside the lens: the four fused bumps came back as an even, horizontal, same-size row centred in an open band, directly above the rock's own grin, which reads as a second row of teeth. v2 said the bumps are 'of noticeably different sizes, tilted on a diagonal, tucked low among the pebbles with the neighbouring pebbles crowding up against and overlapping both of its ends', and made the rock enormous and the handle thick. Attempt 2 fixed the ridge and gave bottom 0.1760 / right 0.0255 but pulled the rock off the left edge (left 0.0000). Per SKILL.md's crop-don't-re-roll rule the attempt-2 RAW png was cropped to box (0,40,1024,960) and re-traced through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths/build_svg. The box was chosen by measuring 34 candidate crops on the COMPOSED .coloring.svg (cairosvg at 500 px, ink fraction in the outermost rows/cols of the top 72% of the page), never on the raw raster.
command: uv run --script .claude/skills/microbe-render/scripts/coloring.py --microbe alh-84001 --set mars-meteorite --prompt-file <prompt_v2> --speech-en "Look as closely as you like — checking is the best part!" --speech-de "Schaut so genau hin, wie ihr wollt — Nachprüfen ist das Beste!" --model gemini-2.5-flash-image --attempt 2

crop.why: attempt 2's rock stopped short of the left edge (left ink 0.0000); cropping 40 px off the top and 64 off the bottom re-scales the art so it bleeds left, right and bottom. Traced locally, no extra API call.

edge_ink.method: cairosvg 500px, outermost rows/cols of the top 72% of the composed .coloring.svg
edge_ink.note: top is 0.0000 by construction on every page in this atlas — the speech bubble owns the top of the frame. Bottom/left/right all sit inside the healthy 0.02-0.27 band. Frame check: densest outer 8-row/col band peaks at 0.117, nowhere near a solid border.
